page.layout: One column of italic verse, set full width, with a catchword ("Tum") at the lower right. The running head is at the top. No page number is printed.

l.i: Ofite quis iam manet exitus ante Videres:
Nam tibi mox gemitum & lacrymas, miserofq;
Ululatus,
Ultrices furias & ineluctabile fatum
Attulerit iam summa dies tibi fera gementi.
Ride age, terrarumque nefas crimenque Sodon
Impia. Quod si nunc caeli te languida claudo
Securum vindicta gradu sequiturve premitve,
Ingenti nec adhuc ferri trabe frangit auaros
Pontifices, miserumque istum infamemq; Diali
Quae nimium, heu nimium funesta Lutetia nouii
Hoc mage terribilem spera scelerata ruinam.
Sera pedes lanea instar habet vindicta, sed acre
Ingeminans ictus, & ferrea brachia quassans
Ter populos: pede profubigit calcatque tiaras
Pontificum Regumque, magistratusque superbos
Eratus quondam audaces qui frontibus auden-
Insultare Deo, & lentum irridere furorem
Numinis, & cornu caelum pulsare feroci.
Sic ubi Vulturnus, furiosaque verbera Cori
Procumbunt pelago (quum matutinus Orion
Occidit) ecce ater rapido furit impete fluctus,
Et vanum exultans, praeceps vehit agmè aquarum
Arduus, ac longo rupem se murmure contra
Impatiens agit: at mediis, elusus, in undis
Frangitur examinis, scopuloque refusus in aquor[?]
Dilabens perit ille furor, saxoque latranti
Laguidus immoritur, sanaque obmurmurat ira:
Ergo Deus populos, metuendaque nomina Reges

page.notes: Right edge of the page is cut off; the last letters of lines 17, 23, 26 and 27 are partly lost, and "auden-" continues beyond the scan. Doubtful: "Ter" (line 15, the first word looks like Rer), "novii" (line 11), "Laguidus" (line 28, possibly Languidus), "aquor" (line 26, possibly aequor). The initial "Ride" may read "Vide" but the letter looks like R. The catchword "Tum" is set at the lower right and is not repeated in the text.
